lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met odd and even numbers. Is 15 odd or even? Odd: it ends in 5.
A pattern follows a rule. Start at 3 and add 4: 3, 7, 11, 15, 19… Each number is 4 more than the one before.
Some rules multiply. Start at 2 and double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32…
Shapes can grow in patterns too. These towers grow by 2 blocks each time: 2, 4, 6… The next tower has 8.
Look for things the rule does not say. Start at 1 and add 2: 1, 3, 5, 7… Every number is odd, because adding 2 to an odd number gives another odd number.
Try it in the world: build a staircase where each step is 2 blocks higher than the last. How tall is step 6? The rule: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Next: equal fractions.

exercises.hint: Check the rule on every step, not just the first.

exercises.prompt: Start at 7 and add 7 each time. What is the 10th number?
Start at 2 and add 4: 2, 6, 10, 14… All the numbers are even.
exercises.hint: Adding an even number to an even number gives an even number.
exercises.explain: 2 is even and 4 is even, so every number is even.

exercises.prompt: Start at 1 and multiply by 3: 1, 3, 9, 27… Which is true?
choices: They take turns odd and even
exercises.hint: An odd number times an odd number is odd.
exercises.explain: 1 is odd, and odd × 3 is always odd.

exercises.prompt: Each row of a pyramid has 2 fewer blocks than the row below. The bottom row has 15. How many blocks are in the 5th row from the bottom?
The towers grow by the same number each time. How many blocks will the next tower have?
exercises.hint: How many blocks are added each time?
exercises.explain: 1, 3, 5: they grow by 2, so the next has 7.

exercises.prompt: Match each pattern to its rule.
exercises.hint: Look at how you get from each number to the next.
